To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genetic basis of RSA in maize is stage dependent and that the root traits at stage I are the most important for GY.
the genetic basis of RSA in maize is stage-specific.
root establishment at the seedling stage is closely related with GY, which can be used as a selection criterion for maize improvement in the field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic architecture of root system architecture and its relationship to grain yield in the field, which is of great interest for maize breeders to improve root growth in field conditions.
the development of maize lines with better RSA for improved yield in the future.
the genetic control of maize root architecture in the field, and it provides useful information for further studies of the genetic control of RSA in maize.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
root development is controlled by a large number of genes, and the genetic control of root growth is more complex than that of shoot traits.
the genetic architecture of RSA is complex and the genetic basis of RSA under field conditions remains to be elucidated.
the genetic control of RSA is a complex process and is affected by the environment, and that root traits are important for GY, particularly for root establishment at the seedling stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QTLs for GY and root traits are located in different genomic regions, which indicates the possibility of improving GY by manipulating root traits.
the root establishment in the seedling stage was important for grain yield and QTLs for the RSA traits were identified at different developmental stages.

(1) root establishment in the field is a key factor for maize yield; (2) the QTLs detected in our study could be used as reference for marker-assisted breeding to improve RSA and yield; (3) the QTL mapping in different developmental stages could provide a better understanding for the genetic basis of RSA in maize.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to evaluate the root system architecture of a plant under field conditions, and that this evaluation should be conducted at the seedling stage.
root traits are important for maize yield and can be improved by breeding.
root establishment at the seedling stage is a key factor to improve GY in maize.
